reason: The cited evidence shows that laser cladding can deposit HEA+WC coatings with good bonding (E4), but it does not address hot-cracking resistance or HAZ reduction for repair. E1 and E2 demonstrate hot cracking in arc-welded HEAs, which supports the problem but not the proposed solution. E3 is about bending tests and does not support the key premises. Thus, the specific claims about crack resistance, HAZ reduction, and superiority over fusion welding lack direct support.
premises: Laser cladding of HEA+WC produces a crack-resistant, dual-phase repair layer
Rapid cooling in laser cladding minimizes thermal gradients and reduces hot cracking
WC reinforcement improves wear resistance and inhibits crack propagation
The repair layer has a narrow heat-affected zone (HAZ)
The HEA+WC cladding outperforms traditional fusion welding in crack resistance and mechanical properties
